notes:
GAMbit now has a built-in assistant called the Helper. Open it with 💬 Helper in the top bar or F2. If someone types a full sentence into the top search box, that goes to the Helper too. All 266 tests pass, the click-through test turned up no new errors, and the Windows build includes the Helper.

What it does

Understands everyday wording and typos. “reset passwrd for jane”, “can you lock jdoe’s acount” and “what grups is jane doe in” all work. It also knows school wording like kid, teacher, lock, out of office and “won’t turn on”.
Fills in details from your directory. It finds people by name or email, plus groups, org units, serials and asset tags. If something is missing it asks (“Who is it for?”). If two people share a first name it asks which one. “Her” or “them” means the last person mentioned.
Finds the right page and lists its steps.
Walks people through a page. It opens the page and shows Step 1 of N with Back and Next. Show me switches to the tab the step names and highlights the button.
Writes GAM commands for about 35 common jobs: passwords, suspend, move, sign-out, 2-step verification, groups, aliases, forwarding, out of office, Drive transfer, and Chromebook look-ups and actions. Each command is checked against GAM’s own command list and labelled “changes things” or “only reads”.
Explains any GAM command someone pastes in.
Nothing runs until someone clicks Run. A run still goes through the person’s role, help-desk mode, dry run and approvals. Commands that make changes ask for confirmation first. Each command also has Copy and Edit in Console, and the Helper never offers pages the person’s role can’t open.

Optional local AI. The ⚙ button in the Helper sets up an AI that answers open-ended questions, using the Guide as background. It runs only on that PC, so nothing typed leaves the computer. It’s a one-time download (about 2 GB, or 1 GB for a smaller version), and the standard version needs about 8 GB of memory. The files can be copied in from a USB stick instead, and an existing Ollama install also works. Commands the AI writes get the same check and are labelled as written by the AI.

Things to know

I’ve only tested the local AI against a stand-in server. The real download and model haven’t been run, so try Test it in ⚙ on a real PC first.
The command check confirms GAM recognises the start of a command, not every option after it. Commands from the AI should still be read before running.
If a question mixes in a school name that the Guide never mentions (like “Lincoln”), the Helper may give a short list of likely pages instead of one answer.
The Guide has a new article, “The Helper (offline assistant)”, and I’ve updated the project notes.
